newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Vietnam, Cambodia sign pact, discuss border.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam, Cambodia sign pact, discuss border.

text.p: Vietnamese Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam flew home on Friday after discussing the thorny issues of immigration and the border with Cambodia and signing a bilateral cooperation pact aimed at strengthening ties.
He paid courtesy calls on National Assembly president Chea Sim and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on Friday before leaving for Vietnam, a Vietnamese diplomat said, without giving details of the talks.
The minister met with his counterpart Ung Huot on Thursday for a signing ceremony and talks, which included their border and immigration issues.

"We have decided to continue this discussion on Vietnamese nationals and the border. We have had some successes in resolving the (problems) and now we will continue to accelerate the discussion...to resolve the problems, the sooner the better," the diplomat told reporters.
He added that after signing the agreement on cooperation and a consular accord, Cambodia had agreed to buy electricity from Vietnam, but he did not specify under what terms.

The two nations also agreed to consider educational exchanges to promote Cambodia's entry into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), to promote technical cooperation in agriculture and irrigation, and to form a telecommunications committee that will work to install fibre-optic cable links.
The countries vowed to sign a trade agreement in 1997 and improve road and waterway links in the future.
Two-way trade between Cambodia and Vietnam has increased from $85 million in 1995 to $110 million in 1996, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
But officials conceded the neighbours have not entirely erased the strains of their troubled ties over the past 200 years, including differences over ethnic Vietnamese living in Cambodia.
Co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who fought against the 1979-89 Vietnamese military presence in Cambodia, has formed a political coalition that has accused Vietnam of border incursions.
The two foreign ministers said disagreements over their 1,130-kilometre (700-mile) border would not be solved overnight, but that they were making progress.
